# zugrpc

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zugrpc/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zugrpc/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedrobtz/zugrpc/gh-pages/badges/coverage.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zugrpc/actions/workflows/coverage.yaml)

## Overview

[gRPC](https://grpc.io) is how many services talk to each other, Spark
Connect among them. It runs only over HTTP/2 and puts each call's status in
HTTP trailers, which the usual R HTTP clients do not expose. Until now,
calling a gRPC service from R meant installing the gRPC C++ libraries or
going through Python.

zugrpc is a gRPC client written in R. It speaks the gRPC wire protocol over
the HTTP/2 requests that [zuhttp](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuhttp)
makes, so it needs no gRPC, protobuf or libcurl installed on the system.
You encode and decode messages yourself, typically with
[zuproto](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuproto).

* **Unary and server-streaming calls.** `grpc_call()` returns one message;
  `grpc_stream()` returns them one at a time as they arrive, and the server
  sends only as fast as you read.
* **Errors you can select by class.** Every status code is a condition
  class, such as `zugrpc_error_unavailable`, and the `google.rpc.Status`
  details, Spark's `ErrorInfo` among them, are decoded for you.
* **Deadlines and cancellation.** A deadline goes to the server as
  `grpc-timeout` and also bounds the call locally. Cancelling a stream
  resets it with `RST_STREAM` and keeps the connection for other calls.
* **zuhttp's transport.** Cleartext HTTP/2 for local servers, TLS with the
  platform's own TLS stack and trust store, a connection pool and HTTP/2
  keepalive.

## Installation

zugrpc is not on CRAN yet. Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zugrpc")
```

## Usage

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(zugrpc)
```

```{r fake-server, include = FALSE}
# A fake gRPC server, so that this README renders anywhere: zuhttp's mock
# transport answers each request as a server would, framing included.
frame <- function(text) {
  bytes <- charToRaw(text)
  n <- length(bytes)
  c(as.raw(c(0, n %/% 2^24, n %/% 2^16 %% 256, n %/% 256 %% 256, n %% 256)), bytes)
}
answer <- function(req) {
  ok <- function(body) {
    zuhttp::zu_response(
      200L,
      headers = c("content-type" = "application/grpc+proto"),
      body = body,
      trailers = c("grpc-status" = "0")
    )
  }
  switch(
    sub(".*/", "", req$url),
    SayHello = ok(frame(paste0("hello, ", rawToChar(req$body[-(1:5)])))),
    Count = ok(do.call(c, lapply(c("one", "two", "three"), frame))),
    zuhttp::zu_response(
      200L,
      headers = c(
        "content-type" = "application/grpc+proto",
        "grpc-status" = "5",
        "grpc-message" = "no%20such%20greeting"
      )
    )
  )
}
fake <- zuhttp::zu_client(transport = zuhttp::zu_mock_transport(answer))
```

These examples talk to a fake server, built from zuhttp's mock transport,
with plain-text messages instead of protobuf. Against a real server, leave
out `client = fake`.

A channel holds what every call to one server shares.

```{r}
ch <- grpc_channel("http://localhost:50051", client = fake)
```

A unary call sends one request message and returns one response.

```{r}
res <- grpc_call(ch, "/demo.Greeter/SayHello", charToRaw("world"), deadline = 5)
rawToChar(res$message)
```

A server-streaming call yields its messages one at a time, then `NULL`.

```{r}
st <- grpc_stream(ch, "/demo.Greeter/Count", raw())
while (!is.null(m <- st$next_message())) print(rawToChar(m))
st$status()
```

A failed call raises a condition whose class names its status.

```{r}
tryCatch(
  grpc_call(ch, "/demo.Greeter/SayGoodbye", raw()),
  zugrpc_error_not_found = function(cnd) cnd$grpc_message
)
```

Every function starts with `grpc_`, except `zugrpc_info()`, and a failed
call's condition class is `zugrpc_error_` followed by its status code in
lower case.

## Learn more

* [Get started](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zugrpc/articles/zugrpc.html)
  walks through channels, calls, streams, errors and cancellation.
* [Performance](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zugrpc/articles/performance.html)
  reports what zugrpc adds to a call, measured.
* The [function reference](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zugrpc/reference/)
  documents every function.

## Related work

zugrpc follows gRPC's
[HTTP/2 protocol](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/PROTOCOL-HTTP2.md)
and [status codes](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/statuscodes.md).
It is tested against [grpc-go](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-go)'s interop
server and against [Spark Connect](https://spark.apache.org/spark-connect/).
It bundles the `google/rpc` protocol definitions from
[googleapis](https://github.com/googleapis/googleapis) to decode error
details. [rgrpc](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=rgrpc) is a client
and server built on the gRPC C++ libraries.
